description: 🚀 I'm a third-year Electrical & Electronics Engineering student from India, passionate about space exploration, robotics, electronics and innovation. I'm leading LUNAR NEXUS to develop an interactive lunar mission-planning simulator for NASA Space Apps 2026 (CH-04). I'm looking for enthusiastic teammates skilled in Unity, VR, Python, AI, 3D modelling, data analysis and space science. Beginners with creativity and dedication are welcome. Let's build something extraordinary together! 🌕
summary: LUNA-SCOPE is an interactive lunar landing-site exploration platform that helps users understand the challenges of selecting potential landing regions on the Moon. It combines interactive 2D and 3D lunar views, candidate-site exploration, sunlight analysis, side-by-side comparisons, a mission scenario simulator, and a VR-style viewing experience. By bringing these features together, the project makes lunar terrain and illumination conditions easier to explore and understand. It is designed as an educational and exploratory decision-support prototype for students, researchers, and space enthusiasts. LUNA-SCOPE uses curated lunar references and simplified analytical models, and does not claim to provide live NASA data or certified landing-site recommendations.
details:
LUNA-SCOPE: Beyond Earth, Into the Future of Lunar Exploration

What if you could stand in the middle of a lunar mission control room and explore the Moon like a scientist, an engineer, and a future astronaut?

That is the idea behind LUNA-SCOPE.

LUNA-SCOPE is an interactive 3D Lunar Landing Site Navigator designed to help users explore the Moon, investigate potential landing locations, understand lunar environmental conditions, and experience some of the challenges involved in planning a lunar mission.

Instead of simply showing pictures and facts about the Moon, we wanted to build something more powerful: a platform where users can actually interact with the lunar surface, examine locations, compare potential landing sites, and experiment with different mission scenarios.

1. What Does LUNA-SCOPE Actually Do?

LUNA-SCOPE brings several lunar exploration capabilities together in one interactive platform.

  • Interactive 3D Moon: Explore a three-dimensional lunar globe, rotate it, zoom in, and investigate the Moon's surface.
  • 2D Lunar Map: Navigate lunar regions and explore marked locations using an interactive map.
  • Lunar Site Analysis: Investigate potential landing locations and examine factors such as sunlight conditions, surface characteristics, and environmental considerations.
  • Site Comparison: Compare different lunar locations to understand their advantages and challenges before selecting a potential landing region.
  • Mission Simulator: Experiment with different dates, times, locations, and hypothetical mission conditions through our What-If Simulator.
  • Lunar Lighting and Sunlight Simulation: Explore how sunlight and illumination conditions change across selected locations and times.
  • VR Exploration Mode: Experience an immersive preview of the lunar environment with stereo viewing controls, adjustable field of view, IPD settings, gaze interaction, and gyroscope options.

2. How Does It Work?

Imagine you are part of a team planning a mission to the Moon.

Where should the spacecraft land? Will the landing region receive enough sunlight? What environmental challenges might astronauts and equipment face?

LUNA-SCOPE allows users to investigate these questions through interactive maps, 3D visualizations, location analysis, and simulation tools.

Users can select lunar locations, explore their surroundings, examine illumination conditions, compare sites, and experiment with hypothetical scenarios.

The platform uses locally embedded lunar reference information and scientific datasets inspired by missions and research including NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), LOLA, LROC, Apollo, Chandrayaan-3, Chang'e-4, and Artemis-related studies.

Its calculations and visualizations run directly in the browser using embedded information, allowing the application to operate without depending on live API connections.

3. What Makes It Innovative?

The real innovation is bringing multiple lunar exploration activities into one accessible digital environment.

Traditional educational resources often explain lunar exploration through separate images, documents, and scientific information. LUNA-SCOPE takes a different approach by allowing users to interact with a virtual lunar environment and investigate mission-planning considerations themselves.

It combines 3D visualization, geographical exploration, scientific references, analytical tools, hypothetical simulations, and an immersive VR preview into a single platform.

We wanted to move beyond simply teaching people about space and give them an opportunity to explore how space missions are planned.

4. Technology Used

LUNA-SCOPE was developed using modern web technologies:

  • TypeScript: Application logic and structured development.
  • React: Interactive user interface and application components.
  • Vite: Development and production build system.
  • Three.js and WebGL: Real-time 3D lunar visualization.
  • HTML, CSS and SVG/Canvas: Interface design, maps, and visualizations.
  • Cloudflare Pages: Public deployment and hosting.

The application is designed to run locally in the browser, with embedded reference data and no dependency on live external APIs.

5. Benefits and Intended Impact

LUNA-SCOPE aims to make lunar exploration more understandable and accessible.

Its potential benefits include:

  • Helping students understand lunar geography and space exploration.
  • Encouraging interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).
  • Demonstrating the importance of sunlight, surface conditions, and location selection in lunar mission planning.
  • Providing an interactive environment for exploring hypothetical mission scenarios.
  • Making complex space-related concepts easier to visualize.
  • Inspiring future researchers, engineers, astronauts, and space enthusiasts.

6. Creativity and Team Considerations

Our team approached this project with one central question:

How can we turn the complex process of exploring and planning a lunar mission into an interactive experience that anyone can understand?

We focused on creating an engaging interface while considering usability, scientific context, accessibility, responsiveness, visualization performance, and the ability to operate offline.

We also considered how the platform could grow in the future through additional scientific datasets, improved environmental models, and more advanced immersive exploration capabilities.

7. Our Vision

LUNA-SCOPE is more than a digital map of the Moon. It is a step towards making space exploration interactive, understandable, and accessible to everyone.

We believe the future of space exploration belongs not only to astronauts and scientists, but also to the students and young innovators who dream of reaching beyond Earth.

We explored the Moon through code. We turned scientific information into an experience. And we built LUNA-SCOPE with one goal: to bring the future of lunar exploration a little closer to everyone.

LUNA-SCOPE — Explore the Moon. Analyze the Unknown. Imagine Beyond Earth.
